record.one_liner: E-commerce platform (Magento, sold as Adobe Commerce) with REST and GraphQL APIs.
record.auth_notes: Cloud Service (SaaS) REST uses Adobe IMS OAuth 2 (server-to-server or user flow); the docs say token generation is not supported in SaaS. PaaS/on-prem uses integration tokens (api_key). Third-party apps on the REST API use OAuth 1.0a, which is classed as other.
record.access_notes: Unverified. The fetched getting-started page shows sandbox instances for development and testing, but it does not say whether sandboxes are free or whether API credentials need a paid Cloud Service licence. A search snippet listed a licence as a prerequisite, but I did not open that page. Set to paid_plan with low confidence because no free API path was verified, pending a check of licensing.
record.api_notes: Cloud Service REST endpoints differ significantly from PaaS/on-prem, and the docs point to GraphQL for similar functionality. Breadth was not measured against an endpoint list.
record.blocker_notes: The fetched docs show a token-free SaaS path is not available and point to Adobe IMS credentials. Whether a free developer path exists depends on licensing, which I did not verify. The official MCP is a developer-tooling server for building apps, not a store-data API server. Community MCP servers for store data exist (for example github.com/magendooro/magemcp).

evidence.quote: Adobe Commerce as a Cloud Service REST API authentication is handled through Adobe's Identity Management System (IMS) through standardized OAuth 2 protocols.
In previous versions of Adobe Commerce, you would use authentication tokens to authorize your requests to the REST API.
Sandbox instances are for design and testing purposes only.
access to similar functionality remains available with the GraphQL APIs.
Instead, you must obtain an IMS admin token through OAuth authentication.
